scope: Finish primitive identity/lifecycle/guarantee/reducibility audit before application-model design. Classify concepts and test current behavioral boundaries; no generalized assessment API, new application model, identity migration or broad product-conformance claim.
criteria: Independent identity and what must survive change
Mutable lifecycle versus immutable historical fact
Essential validation, capture, concurrency and recovery guarantees
Constructive existing-structure encoding and rules needed for equivalent behavior
Observable counterexamples and explicit limits; implementation inconvenience is not proof of conceptual irreducibility

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Native UUID and individually versioned managed state
inventory.reduction: Project record types specialize this contract; arbitrary fields cannot replace guarded identity/version/history.

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Link UUID independent of endpoints/type; native versions
inventory.reduction: An entity encoding is possible, but must restore direction, endpoint integrity, parallel-link identity and traversal semantics. Endpoint fields alone are lossy.
inventory.decision: retain contract; no mathematical irreducibility claim

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Schema versions, exact object revisions and atomic commit identity
inventory.reduction: JSON/timestamps do not themselves enforce schema permissions, exact reconstruction or all-or-nothing history.

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Same native entity UUID; optional exact external source binding; supported promotion
inventory.reduction: Already expressed as entity.resource with @resource for unclassified identities; managed classification can be added without a second identity.

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Binding shares entity identity; locator is mutable location through observations
inventory.reduction: Paths, labels and hashes cannot substitute for stable exact ownership. Legacy binding and resource capability remain compatible; no bulk merge.

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Same relationship UUID/history; distinct uses can share endpoints
inventory.reduction: Already qualified by reference metadata; each excerpt need not become an entity. Removing role/scope/pin loses required meaning.
Values identify kind/scope and current or exact selected state. Unsupported data stays preserved and unresolved; no new entity identity needed.

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Observation ID and append-only provenance; source state separate from native version
inventory.reduction: Shares immutable evidence storage; cannot infer external availability/content from entity metadata or treat observed bytes as engineering acceptance.

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Receipt ID, captured output/declared inputs/outcome/provenance; explicit supersession
inventory.reduction: Can be represented by generic immutable assessment data with typed subject/basis/result, but must preserve exact capture/scoped comparison and outcome. Ordinary mutable records plus text alone do not supply those services.

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Review ID, receipt comparison/token, decision/rationale/provenance; renewed applicability after relevant change
inventory.reduction: Constructive conceptual mapping to assessment: subject=receipt+comparison token, basis=captured comparison, result=decision+rationale. A generic implementation is not executed or proven here; current receipt input vocabulary cannot target this subject.
inventory.decision: not a peer foundational primitive; retain typed guarded operation

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Immutable capture ID, selected exact native revisions; may mix versions
inventory.reduction: Builds on native history. Selection does not establish complete project/commit topology.

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: Immutable baseline ID and exact native commit/schema/topology
inventory.reduction: Builds on native history. A selected member list must add complete atomic commit guarantees to be equivalent; capture does not include external bytes or evidence timeline.

inventory.identityAndLifecycle: View has editable recipe version; read projection has scoped context
inventory.reduction: Recipe is not a state pin; projections are bounded/paged results, not another engineering truth store.

reviewAlternatives.alternative: Plain managed record or execution outcome saying accepted
reviewAlternatives.finding: Tested: no comparison-scoped review is inferred. Version pinning can preserve bytes but comparison targeting and guarded applicability rules remain necessary.

reviewAlternatives.alternative: General immutable assessment with typed subject/basis/result
reviewAlternatives.finding: Conceptually expresses review and execution while retaining specialized services. Review subject is a receipt comparison, not the receipt API current native/content/relationship inputs.
reviewAlternatives.status: conceptual reduction supported; executable API unification not claimed

reviewAlternatives.alternative: Existing typed payloads/commands over shared immutable evidence persistence
reviewAlternatives.finding: Tested shared append-only trigger protection and native/evidence history separation; existing comparison and transaction services preserve scoped semantics.

behavioralEvidence: Promotion preserves one resource/entity identity, reference target/history and scoped external input meaning.
Different passages retain separate link identities on the same source/target pair.
Plain accepted text and generic receipt outcome produce no applicability review.
Stale review token rejects without any export change; accepted changed review retains drift and the exact captured comparison.
Explicit external source change retires earlier review applicability; missing source prevents acceptance without writes.
Observations, receipts and reviews reject direct storage update/delete through the same immutable mechanism and do not allocate native revisions.
A selected configuration and a baseline retain exact older states while current records change; a saved live recipe does not pin native states.
verificationHistory: Initial comparison-shape assertion included absent keys as explicit undefined. Corrected fixture assertion destructures derived response fields before comparing the stored comparison; no product behavior changed.
limits: Finite contract audit, not a mathematical proof of globally optimal/minimal primitives.
Current API substitution failures do not establish fundamental irreducibility. A generalized assessment representation is a conceptual alternative, not a verified replacement implementation.
No runtime, wire, storage format, historical payload, native identity or product requirement acceptance changed.
No standards conformity, representative-user validation, other-backend parity or authenticated team-readiness claim.
Complete application-model work remains pending under the active goal; primitive audit completion does not close that larger objective.
nextBoundary: Application-model work may now distinguish structural objects/history, capabilities and specialized capture services. It must preserve those guarantees and use concrete semantic/composition gaps to justify changes; do not implement a generic assessment engine merely to reduce type names.
